newsitem.title: USA: Danbury, Conn., rated AA by Fitch.
newsitem.headline: Danbury, Conn., rated AA by Fitch.

text.p: NEW YORK, July 25 - Danbury, CT.'s $10.1 million general obligation bonds, issue of 1997, are rated 'AA' by Fitch.

The bonds will be offered for competitive sale July 29, 1997. Dated Aug. 1, 1997, the bonds will mature serially Aug. 1, 1998-2017. Bonds maturing on or after Aug. 1, 2008 are callable at 102% and declining thereafter. In addition, the city's $54.2 million outstanding general obligation bonds are affirmed at 'AA'.

The bonds are general obligations of the city, for which it pledges its full faith and credit. Bond proceeds will be used to permanently finance bond anticipation notes (BANs) issued for various projects in the city's capital plan and water system improvements. Danbury continues to be an important regional employment and retail center, maintaining a solid foundation of employment and economic activity. The services sector provided 28% of employment in 1996 and the trade and manufacturing sectors 26% and 23%, respectively. About 56% of the city's employed residential labor force work in Danbury, a testament to the city's status as an employment center.

Unemployment rates are lower than the state and nation. Assessed valuation has grown steadily and the value of new building permits, fueled by commercial development, rose 37% to $38.2 million in 1996. Wealth levels are generally above those of the state and nation. The city's $48,562 median household income in 1995 was 110% of the state level and 151% of the national average. Net debt levels continue to be low and the capital improvement plan is modest, as the city's infrastructure is generally in place. Net direct debt is $667 per capita and 0.7% of the full value of property. Payout of all debt is rapid. Financial performance is solid, as the city has managed its resources while funding landfill closure on a pay-as-you-go basis.

Tax collection rates continue to improve, matching pre- recession levels. For fiscal year 1997, the city estimates an unreserved, undesignated fund balance of $5.8 million -- a healthy 4.4% of general fund expenditures. The fiscal 1998 budget reflects conservative revenue and expenditure estimates. The city anticipates a year end fund balance of $11.7 million from the expected receipt of a $10 million up front payment from contracting out operations of its sewer system to a private operator. The payment will replenish the general fund for past landfill expenditures.
